# Grid: content-sized cells measure their wrapped text in place

## Context

This is leaf L2 of epic #19658, blocked by #19661 (the geometry model). Mounted rows get their real heights by measuring the displayed text in place.

## The Problem

Content-sized mode needs each mounted row's natural height: the maximum across its declared wrapping text columns, in every body. The constrained outer row and cell are not a natural-content oracle, because cells inherit the row's height and rows are `contain: strict`.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The cell:** `.neo-grid-cell` is `display: flex`, `align-items: center`, `height: inherit`, `padding: 2px 10px 2px`, with 1px bottom and right borders, `border-box` (`Body.scss`).
- **The flex trap (epic review, Stage 4):** inside a flex cell, a block child is a flex item, and its automatic minimum width is its longest word. `overflow-wrap: break-word` then never breaks a long word, which overflows instead. D#19645 probe 2 showed that a flex cell missed 43 of 900 cases and a block cell missed 0.
- **The read:** `DomAccess.getLayoutRect({id: [...]})` measures transform-immune layout boxes in one batch with one forced layout.

## The Fix

- **Declared columns:** a column flag (name settled at intake, e.g. `wrapText: true`) declares a height-driving text column.
- **The text container:** in content-sized mode a declared cell renders its text in a block container with `white-space: normal`, `overflow-wrap: break-word` and `height: auto`. Either the cell becomes `display: block` in this mode, or the container gets `min-width: 0; flex: 1 1 auto`, so long words break.
- **The measurement:** after a mount or update, the App Worker requests the layout rects of the mounted text containers in one batch. It adds the cell's vertical padding and border, takes the maximum per row across columns and bodies, and feeds #19661's height setter.
- **The generation fence:** each request carries a view/record/layout generation (content, width and font context), and a response whose generation no longer matches is dropped. Recycled slots never write a stale record.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback / edge case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Column flag declaring a height-driving text column | #19658 | Only declared columns drive height; others take the row height | Without declared columns, rows keep the estimate | JSDoc | Unit + e2e |
| Content-sized cell CSS | Epic review Stage 4 | Long words break inside the column width | — | SCSS comment | Spec with a word longer than the column |
| Measurement generation fence | D#19645 (Sophie 18878897) | Stale responses are dropped | — | JSDoc | Recycled-slot spec |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A declared column's wrapped text gives the row its natural height; the row height is the maximum across declared columns in all three bodies.
- [x] A word longer than the column width breaks inside the cell instead of overflowing; this is a spec.
- [x] A measurement that returns after the slot was recycled to another record, or after a width or content change, does not update geometry; this is a spec.
- [x] Mounted rows need one batched layout read per update, not one per row.
- [x] With the mode off, nothing in this leaf runs.

## Out of Scope

Rows and columns not yet mounted, measure-ahead, and font-arrival invalidation (L3); scroll correction (L4).

## Avoided Traps

- Measuring the constrained row or cell box, which only reports its imposed height.
- A per-row main-thread `ResizeObserver` that writes heights: the App Worker owns geometry, and main only reports observations.
- Calling a stateful renderer a second time just to size it.

The candidate alternative, `DomAccess#getNaturalRect` (it releases an inline height and reads the box in one task), cannot read a row's natural height: rows are `contain: strict` and cells take `height: inherit` from CSS, not from an inline style (`Body.scss`). ### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-10-12T15:19:29Z

**Implemented** on `ada/19662-measure-wrapped-text` at `b2e93715a3`, stacked on #19668. The PR opens against dev after #19668 merges, so the block on #19661 stays in force until then.

- **AC-1:** unit `grid/WrapTextMeasure.spec.mjs` › "rows take their tallest wrapText column across bodies…". The wrap columns sit in the start and center bodies. e2e `grid/WrapTextMeasure.spec.mjs` › "every row is as tall as its tallest wrapped text, in each body" compares each row's rect with its text container plus the computed cell chrome.
- **AC-2:** e2e › "a word longer than its column breaks inside the cell". Negative control: without `min-width: 0` the word overflows the cell and the arm turns red.
- **AC-3:** unit › "a reply for a cell its row rendered again in the meantime is dropped…" holds the read in flight and changes the record. The fence is the cell's vdom node identity plus its width, since a re-render makes a new node. Mutation: without the fence the arm turns red.
- **AC-4:** one `getLayoutRect` batch covers the new text containers of all bodies per pass, and already measured nodes are not read again.
- **AC-5:** unit › "without contentSizedRows, a wrapText column renders and measures nothing".

Deltas I'll carry into the PR:
- Rows never get shorter than `rowHeight`, so columns that don't wrap keep their space.
- Heights are kept per column, so a column scrolled out horizontally keeps its share.
- A row's own update (a record change) triggers a pass too. Mutation-checked with an isolated arm.
- The cell chrome comes from one `getComputedStyle` read per pass.
- Toggling `wrapText` forgets the measured heights.

- 2026-10-12T19:45:17Z @tobiu referenced in commit `07b84f9` - "feat(grid): content-sized rows measure the wrapped text of wrapText columns (#19662) (#19672)

* feat(grid): opt-in content-sized rows read one row geometry per view (#19661)

`contentSizedRows` on grid.Container gives each row its own height. One
Neo.grid.RowGeometry per view (record-id-keyed heights, Float64Array prefix
offsets, binary-search lookup) replaces index x rowHeight for row heights and
transforms, the start row, the visible and mounted rows, both scroll extents
and keyboard scrolling. View#setRowHeights is the internal setter the
measurement leaves will feed.

- An order change (sort, filter, load, mutation, new estimate) runs the full
  pass, which resolves every record id: about 10 ms for 100k rows, skipped
  while no height is known. A height batch patches its rows and sums the
  offsets again from the first changed one: about 0.2 ms for 100k rows.
- The full pass reads store.items, since getAt() hydrates every lazy record.
- The geometry's store listeners run before the bodies' own (order: 'before'),
  so a body re-rendering on the store's load reads fresh offsets.
- A row finds its moved geometry itself (Row#hasStaleGeometry) and re-renders
  with cell recycling instead of a forced full render.
- Content-sized mode re-syncs on every new start row and sizes the pool by the
  smallest row height, so mixed heights never mount more rows than the pool.
- passSizeToBody measures the view. Container minus header also counted the
  borders and the horizontal scrollbar, which left a row that keyboard
  scrolling aligns to the bottom 19px out of sight, in fixed-height grids too.

* feat(grid): content-sized rows measure the wrapped text of wrapText columns (#19662)

In content-sized mode a wrapText column renders its text in a block container
(min-width: 0, so a word longer than the column breaks inside the cell). After
an update of the view, a body or a row lands, View#measureRowHeights reads the
layout boxes of the new containers of all bodies in one batch, adds the cell's
padding and borders, and gives each row its tallest column, never less than
rowHeight.

- Fence: a reply only counts for a cell node its row still renders at the
  width it was read at. A re-render (another record, new content, a new width)
  makes a new node, so the read for the old one is dropped.
- Measured nodes are not read again, so scrolling over measured rows reads
  nothing. Heights are kept per column, so a column scrolled out of the
  mounted range keeps its share of the row.
- Row.setCellId moves a text container's id along with its recycled cell.
- Turning wrapText on or off forgets the measured heights (resetRowHeights).

* fix(grid): a buffered resize after destroy reads no view; class hierarchy lists RowGeometry (#19661)

passSizeToBody now measures the view, and the buffered onResize can reach a
destroyed grid, whose view is null: SplitterHeavyContent's cadence arm got a
pageerror from it (3/3 locally without this). passSizeToBody returns when the
view is gone, and onResize stops after its await once the grid is destroyed.

docs/output/class-hierarchy.json is regenerated (npm run generate-docs-json)
for check-freshness: Neo.grid.RowGeometry, plus the apps/email and
apps/finance entries the tracked file was already missing.

* fix(grid): a replaced store's records start from the estimate, not the old store's heights (#19661)

RowGeometry kept its record-id-keyed heights when the view handed it another
store. With natural keys (useInternalId: false), a different record under a
repeated id then took the old store's height and offset. Heights still
outlive a sort or filter of their store; a new store clears them.

* fix(grid): a replaced store forgets the measured texts of the old store's records (#19662)

Same defect class as #19668's review RA-1: the view's per-column text heights
are keyed by record id, so a new record under a repeated natural id combined
its measured texts with the old record's. bindStore clears them, and the
measured-cell registry, when the store is replaced.

* test(grid): the measurement fence drops replies for recycled slots and changed widths (#19662)

#19662 AC-3 names three cases; the spec covered the content change only. Two
arms hold the read in flight: one recycles every pooled slot to other records,
one changes a recycled cell's width in place. Each fails with its fence
condition removed.

* fix(grid): measured row heights follow hidden cells, removed columns and rowHeight (#19662)

- A cell hidden with display none has no layout box. It is not read, and a reply whose box has no width
  is not kept, so the cell is measured once it shows, also at its unchanged width.
- When a wrapText column leaves the grid, the measured rows drop its text heights and derive their

- A new rowHeight derives the measured rows again from their stored text heights, so the floor applies
